title: Cabinet Refinishing in Hawthorne, FL | Painted Cabinets
description: Cabinet refinishing in Hawthorne, FL: degreased, sanded, primed, and finished in waterborne urethane enamel. Great for older oak kitchens. Free estimate.
heroIntro: Solid oak boxes from an earlier decade are worth keeping. We refinish them with a hard enamel that holds up to humid kitchens and daily handling, for a fraction of the disruption of a tear-out.

sections.h2: Older lake-house kitchens are prime candidates
body: Many of the older homes near Lochloosa and Orange Lake still have their original oak or maple cabinetry. The boxes are usually solid; it is the color and the worn finish that date the room. Our local Hawthorne crews see this kitchen layout often. Cabinet refinishing in Hawthorne, FL keeps the sound wood, skips the demolition, and gives the kitchen a new look in a fraction of the time a remodel takes. Newer SR-20 homes call us for a different reason: builder cabinets in a color the owner never chose.
Still deciding? Our comparison of refinishing versus replacing cabinets walks through the trade-offs.

sections.h2: Grease and humidity: the two enemies
body: Cooking oil builds up invisibly around the range hood, the pulls, and the sink base. A finish laid over that film is only as strong as the grease beneath it. Our crews scrub it off with a cabinet degreaser, rinse with clean water, and scuff-sand until no glossy spots remain; the bonding primer comes after that. In a humid house near the water, we also make sure each coat has the conditions to cure properly before the next one goes on.

Open-grain red oak gets extra attention. Without grain filling, the finished door shows faint stripes under kitchen lighting. With it, the surface reads smooth. Details are in our piece on painting oak cabinets.

bullets: Doors and drawer fronts removed, labelled, and finished away from the boxes
Boxes, face frames, and end panels degreased, scuffed, and finished in place
Bonding primer suited to oak, maple, or thermofoil
Waterborne urethane enamel topcoat that cures hard and wipes clean
Color matched from a chip, an existing door, or a leftover can

sections.h2: Picking a cabinet color that ages well
body: Cabinets are the most-touched painted surface in a house, so color choice is practical as well as aesthetic. Bright whites show grime at the pulls; very dark colors show dust and scratches. Mid-tone neutrals, soft whites with a little warmth, and muted greens or blues are forgiving choices in a busy kitchen. We spray full-size drawdowns so you can see the color in your own light, next to your countertops, before the doors come off.

Bathroom vanities, laundry cabinets, and built-in shelving take the same system. Doing them alongside the kitchen keeps the finish consistent through the house. If you are repainting the walls as well, our Hawthorne interior painting team can schedule both together, and the main cabinet painting and refinishing page has more on our approach.
You keep using the kitchen through most of the project. We protect counters, appliances, and floors, and we tell you in advance which days the boxes will be wet and off-limits.

faqs.q: Can thermofoil or laminate cabinets be painted?
faqs.a: Often, yes, as long as the surface is not peeling or delaminating. A bonding primer made for slick surfaces is used before the enamel.

faqs.q: Will the wood grain show through on oak?
faqs.a: Only if you want it to. Grain filling during prep makes painted oak read smooth; skipping it leaves a visible texture some owners prefer.
We remove and reinstall your existing hardware. If you are switching to new pulls with different hole spacing, tell us during the walkthrough so filling and drilling can be added to the scope.
